s: The first pilot use of an Electronic Voting Machine in India was conducted in which constituency and year?
o: Anantnag Assembly constituency, Jammu and Kashmir, in 1998
x: EVMs were first used on a pilot basis in the 70-Parur Assembly constituency of Kerala in 1982.
tq: Use the exact place-year combination rather than confusing a pilot with a wider trial or statewide use.

s: The wider trial of Electronic Voting Machines in 1998 covered how many Assembly seats in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Delhi?
x: The wider trial in 1998 covered 16 Assembly seats across Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Delhi.
tq: Fix the specific numerical milestone in the EVM timeline.
sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

s: Electronic Voting Machines were used at all polling stations in a Lok Sabha general election for the first time in:
x: The 2004 general election was the first Lok Sabha election in which EVMs were used at all polling stations.
tq: Distinguish nationwide polling-station coverage from the first state-level use.
sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following statements regarding the manufacture and legal framework of EVMs and VVPATs is correct?
o: They are manufactured only by the Election Commission of India under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
They are manufactured by BEL and ECIL, and the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 were amended to permit VVPATs.
They are manufactured by the Reserve Bank of India, and the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 prohibit VVPAT use.
They are manufactured by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, and VVPATs were authorised by the Constitution.
x: Bharat Electronics Limited and Electronics Corporation of India Limited manufacture the machines. The Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 were amended to enable VVPAT use.
tq: Check both the manufacturing bodies and the specific legal instrument instead of accepting a constitutional or ministry attribution.
sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

s: In N. Chandrababu Naidu v. Union of India (2019), VVPAT slips of how many randomly selected EVMs per Assembly segment were directed to be counted?
x: The Supreme Court directed counting of VVPAT slips from five randomly selected EVMs in each Assembly segment.
tq: Identify the court case through its distinctive verification number.
sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Supreme Court's 2024 decision in ADR v. ECI:
1. The demand for ballot paper voting and counting of 100 per cent VVPAT slips was rejected.
2. Symbol-loading units are to be sealed and preserved for 45 days.
3. A runner-up in second or third position may seek checking of 5 per cent of EVMs per segment within seven days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements correctly describe the verification rules associated with ADR v. ECI in April 2024.
tq: Test a cluster of linked judicial safeguards using the coded combination options.
sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

s: VVPAT slips must be counted in which of the following circumstances?
o: Whenever EVM data and Form 17C do not match
Whenever postal ballots exceed the number of EVM votes
Only in constituencies using postal ballots
Only when the winning candidate requests it after the declaration of results
x: VVPAT slips are required to be counted wherever the EVM data and Form 17C do not match.
tq: Apply the verification rule to a specific discrepancy rather than to a general recount demand.
sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following features was specified for EVMs in relation to candidate identification?
o: They must display the candidates' party manifestos.
They must show black-and-white photographs of polling agents.
They must show colour photographs of the candidates.
They must display only the candidates' election symbols without names.
x: EVMs are to display colour photographs of the candidates.
tq: Use the precise official feature and reject nearby but unsupported display requirements.
sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following is the correct order of counting-related procedures?
A. Counting of postal ballots
B. Counting of the penultimate EVM/VVPAT round
C. Counting of the final EVM/VVPAT round
x: Postal ballots are counted before the penultimate EVM/VVPAT round; the final EVM/VVPAT round follows subsequently.
tq: Arrange the procedure by identifying the expressly stated precedence of postal-ballot counting.
sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

s:
With reference to totalisers, consider the following statements:
1. A totaliser combines the counting of several EVMs.
2. It is intended to conceal booth-wise voting trends.
3. The Election Commission has stated that a legal framework for totalisers already exists.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: A totaliser combines several EVM counts to hide booth-wise trends. The ECI stated that no legal framework for totalisers exists, making statement 3 false.
tq: Spot the reversed institutional position in the third statement.
sec: EVM and VVPAT - FIRST use, EVM statements, VVPAT, SC verification rules  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following pairs relating to Delimitation Commissions is NOT correctly matched?
x: The 1973 Commission was chaired by Justice J.L. Kapur. Justice Kuldip Singh chaired the 2002 Commission.
tq: Find the swapped chairperson in a date-person matching question.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the years of the Delimitation Acts from the years in which the corresponding Commissions were constituted?
x: The Delimitation Acts were enacted in 1952, 1962, 1972 and 2002, while the Commissions were constituted in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002.
tq: Separate the closely related years of legislation from the years of constitution of the Commissions.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s:
Read the following statements:
1. Article 82 deals with readjustment of Lok Sabha constituencies after each census.
2. Article 170 deals with readjustment of State Legislative Assembly constituencies after each census.
3. Articles 330 and 332 relate to reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Articles 82 and 170 provide for readjustment relating to Parliament and State Assemblies, while Articles 330 and 332 concern SC/ST seat reservation.
tq: Match constitutional Articles with their institutional subject before selecting the coded combination.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s: Delimitation primarily refers to:
o: Fixing the number of seats and the boundaries of Lok Sabha and Assembly constituencies
Allocating ministerial portfolios among political parties
Determining the expenditure limit of each political party
Preparing the electoral roll for municipal elections only
x: Delimitation is the fixing of the number of seats and boundaries of Lok Sabha and State Assembly constituencies.
tq: Choose the definition that covers both the numerical and territorial aspects of delimitation.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s: The constitutional principle underlying delimitation is best expressed as:
o: One State, one vote, one value
One district, one representative, one value
One party, one constituency, one value
One person, one vote, one value
x: Delimitation rests on the principle of ‘one person, one vote, one value’, associated with uniformity of representation under Article 81(2).
tq: Discriminate among similar-looking formulations of the electoral equality principle.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following statements about the Delimitation Commission is correct?
1. It is constituted under an Act of Parliament.
2. It works with the Election Commission of India.
3. Its orders may be modified by either House of Parliament.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The Commission is constituted under parliamentary legislation and works with the ECI. Its orders cannot be modified by the Lok Sabha or State Legislative Assemblies, so statement 3 is false.
tq: Use the ‘wrong authority’ trap to test who can modify delimitation orders.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following statements regarding the legal status of delimitation orders is correct?
o: They require approval by each State Assembly before becoming effective.
They cannot be challenged in a court and cannot be modified by the Lok Sabha or State Assemblies.
They can be challenged before any High Court as a matter of right.
They can be modified by the Lok Sabha through a simple resolution.
x: Delimitation Commission orders enjoy finality: they cannot be challenged in court or modified by the Lok Sabha or State Legislative Assemblies.
tq: Test the exceptional finality of a statutory Commission’s orders.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s:
Arrange the following Delimitation Commissions in chronological order:
A. Commission chaired by Justice Kuldip Singh
B. Commission chaired by Justice J.L. Kapur constituted in 1963
C. Commission chaired by Justice N. Chandrasekhara Aiyar
D. Commission chaired by Justice J.L. Kapur constituted in 1973
x: The Commissions were constituted in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002 respectively: N. Chandrasekhara Aiyar, J.L. Kapur, J.L. Kapur and Kuldip Singh.
tq: Anchor the sequence to the four constitution years rather than the repeated name of the chairperson.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s: Which Constitutional Amendment froze inter-State allocation of seats until 2000 on the basis of the 1971 Census?
x: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 froze inter-State seat allocation until 2000, using the 1971 Census as the basis.
tq: Link the amendment number with both its year and the census basis.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements about the 84th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2001:
1. It extended the freeze on inter-State seat allocation until after the first census following 2026.
2. It permitted rationalisation of constituencies on the basis of the 1991 Census.
3. It changed the total number of Lok Sabha seats on the basis of the 2001 Census.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The 84th Amendment extended the freeze and allowed rationalisation using the 1991 Census. It did not change the total number of seats on the basis of the 2001 Census.
tq: Separate rationalisation of boundaries from alteration of the total number of seats.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s: The principal effect of the 87th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 was to:
o: Use the 2001 Census for redrawing boundaries without changing the total number of seats
End the freeze on inter-State seat allocation immediately
Restore the 1971 Census as the basis for delimitation and increase total seats
Abolish the Delimitation Commission and transfer its functions to Parliament
x: The 87th Amendment substituted the 2001 Census for boundary redrawing while keeping the total number of seats unchanged.
tq: Distinguish boundary redrawing from an increase in the total seat allocation.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Jammu and Kashmir Delimitation Commission — Justice Ranjana Desai
2. Assam delimitation — Election Commission of India
3. Assam delimitation became effective — August 2023
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The Jammu and Kashmir Commission was headed by Justice Ranjana Desai, while Assam was delimited by the ECI with effect from August 2023.
tq: Combine the authority, chairperson and effective date to avoid state-wise confusion.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s: The orders of the Jammu and Kashmir Delimitation Commission headed by Justice Ranjana Desai became effective in:
x: The Jammu and Kashmir delimitation orders became effective in March and May 2022.
tq: Retain the paired effective months rather than only the year of the Commission’s work.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following statements about the Tamil Nadu Assembly resolution is NOT correct?
o: It proposed freezing the Lok Sabha at 543 seats permanently.
It proposed retaining a 2.2:1 Lok Sabha to Rajya Sabha ratio.
It linked the proposed women’s quota to delimitation from 2029.
It proposed women’s quota from 2029 without linking it to delimitation.
x: The resolution proposed women’s reservation from 2029 without linking it to delimitation. It also proposed a permanent freeze at 543 Lok Sabha seats and retention of the 2.2:1 ratio.
tq: Locate the reversal of an expressly stated condition in a policy-resolution question.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s: The present number of elected Lok Sabha seats, as distinguished from the constitutional ceiling mentioned, is:
x: The Lok Sabha has 543 elected seats against a ceiling of 550, comprising 530 seats for States and 20 for Union Territories in the stated allocation framework.
tq: Distinguish the existing elected strength from the maximum ceiling.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s: The ceiling of 550 Lok Sabha seats mentioned in the constitutional framework consists of:
o: 500 seats for States and 50 seats for Union Territories
543 seats for States and 7 seats for Union Territories
520 seats for States and 30 seats for Union Territories
530 seats for States and 20 seats for Union Territories
x: The stated ceiling comprises 530 seats for the States and 20 seats for the Union Territories.
tq: Break a total into its State and Union Territory components.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s: Since which year have the per-State Lok Sabha seat numbers remained unchanged, as stated in the context of delimitation?
x: The per-State Lok Sabha seat numbers have remained unchanged since 1976.
tq: Separate the year of the constitutional freeze from the census years associated with it.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following statements about the former Anglo-Indian representation in the Lok Sabha is correct?
o: The two Anglo-Indian seats ended in 2020, making the older ceiling description outdated.
The Anglo-Indian seats were transferred to the Rajya Sabha in 2020.
The Anglo-Indian seats were increased from two to twenty in 2020.
The two Anglo-Indian seats continue to form part of the present elected strength.
x: The two Anglo-Indian nominated seats ended in 2020. Therefore, the older description of a maximum of 552 seats including two Anglo-Indians is stale.
tq: Identify the time-sensitive constitutional change behind an outdated numerical claim.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between Articles 81(2), 82 and 170 in delimitation?
o: Article 81(2) expresses uniformity of representation, while Articles 82 and 170 provide for constituency readjustment for Parliament and State Assemblies respectively.
Articles 82 and 170 prescribe the powers of the Election Commission but not constituency readjustment.
Article 81(2) deals only with Panchayat elections, while Articles 82 and 170 concern presidential elections.
Article 82 concerns Rajya Sabha elections and Article 170 concerns municipal elections.
x: Article 81(2) embodies uniformity of representation, while Articles 82 and 170 provide the constitutional basis for readjustment of Lok Sabha and Assembly constituencies.
tq: Map each Article to its distinct constitutional function rather than its broad election subject.
sec: Delimitation - Commissions, Articles 82 and 170, freeze, 84th/87th Amendments  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the NETA app is correct?
o: It enables voters to rate their elected representatives and was built by a private start-up.
It is used exclusively for filing election petitions before the High Courts.
It was conceptualised and developed by the Election Commission of India.
It enables citizens to report Model Code of Conduct violations with geo-tagged photographs.
x: The NETA app allows voters to rate their representatives and was built by a private start-up, not conceptualised by the Election Commission of India.
tq: Distinguish the private NETA app from official Election Commission applications.
sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

s:
Consider the following statements regarding cVIGIL:
1. It enables citizens to report violations of the Model Code of Conduct.
2. Photographs or videos accompanying a complaint may be geo-tagged.
3. The system provides for action within 100 minutes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: cVIGIL enables citizens to report Model Code violations using geo-tagged photographs or videos, with action envisaged within 100 minutes.
tq: Check whether all three operational features belong to the same application.
sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

s: ECINET is associated with which one of the following functions?
o: Merging more than 40 Election Commission applications and websites into one platform
Issuing election petitions directly to the Supreme Court
Providing only postal ballots to service voters
x: ECINET is a unified platform that merges more than 40 Election Commission applications and websites.
tq: Identify the precise institutional function of the named digital platform.
sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

s:
The Voter Helpline app is primarily used for which of the following purposes?
1. Searching for a name in the electoral roll
2. Filing forms and complaints
3. Reporting violations through geo-tagged videos only
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The Voter Helpline app helps users search the electoral roll and file forms and complaints. Reporting Model Code violations through geo-tagged photographs or videos is associated with cVIGIL.
tq: Separate closely related functions of different Election Commission apps.
sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

s:
Which of the following categories of electors are entitled to use postal ballots?
1. Service voters
2. Special voters
3. Electors on election duty
4. Persons in preventive detention
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The listed categories—service voters, special voters, electors on election duty and persons in preventive detention—are covered by postal-ballot provisions.
tq: Test completeness of a statutory-category list rather than recalling a single category.
sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

s: The indelible election ink used in India is manufactured by which organisation and is based on which substance?
o: Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd; silver nitrate
x: Indelible election ink is manufactured by Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd and is based on silver nitrate.
tq: Use the manufacturer–ingredient pair to avoid a two-part factual trap.
sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Voter Helpline app — Search name in electoral roll
ECINET — Exclusive platform for election petitions
x: ECINET is a unified platform merging more than 40 Election Commission applications and websites; it is not an exclusive platform for election petitions.
tq: Find the mismatched purpose among closely related electoral initiatives.
sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

s:
Consider the following measures relating to polling stations:
1. The maximum number of electors assigned to a polling station is 1,200.
2. A facility is provided for depositing mobile phones at polling booths.
3. Candidate booths are to be located just beyond 100 metres from the polling station.
4. Candidate photographs on EVMs have been redesigned in colour.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The measures include a 1,200-elector cap, mobile-deposit facilities, colour candidate photographs on EVMs and candidate booths just beyond 100 metres from polling stations.
tq: Treat each administrative measure as an independent statement and verify the complete set.
sec: Voter facilitation - ECI apps, postal ballot, election ink

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 330 — Reservation of seats for SCs and STs in State Legislative Assemblies
Article 332 — Reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha
Article 330 — Reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha
Article 334 — Establishment of the Election Commission
x: Article 330 provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha, while Article 332 concerns State Legislative Assemblies.
tq: Use the Article–institution pairing and reject neighbouring-Article swaps.

s:
With reference to reserved Lok Sabha constituencies in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Amalapuram is a Scheduled Caste-reserved constituency.
2. Araku is a Scheduled Tribe-reserved constituency.
3. Tirupati is a Scheduled Tribe-reserved constituency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Amalapuram and Tirupati are Scheduled Caste-reserved constituencies in Andhra Pradesh, whereas Araku is the Scheduled Tribe-reserved constituency.
tq: Discriminate between SC and ST constituencies within the same State.
sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

s: Which one of the following correctly represents the reservation pattern in the Lok Sabha for Telangana?
x: Telangana has three Scheduled Caste-reserved and two Scheduled Tribe-reserved Lok Sabha constituencies.
tq: Compare the State-wise SC/ST figures without reversing the categories.
sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

s:

List-I (State)

B. Andhra Pradesh — Legislative Assembly
C. Telangana — Lok Sabha
D. Telangana — Legislative Assembly

List-II (Number of SC/ST reserved seats)
1. 4 / 1
2. 29 / 7
3. 3 / 2
4. 19 / 12

Code:
x: Andhra Pradesh has 4 SC and 1 ST Lok Sabha seats and 29 SC and 7 ST Assembly seats. Telangana has 3 SC and 2 ST Lok Sabha seats and 19 SC and 12 ST Assembly seats.
tq: Start with the sure State–House pair and then complete the numerical matching.
sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the allocation of SC and ST reserved constituencies?
1. ST seats are generally located where the share of the ST population is highest.
2. SC seats are spread across the State and rotated at each delimitation.
3. All voters in a reserved constituency, and not merely voters belonging to the reserved community, may vote.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: ST seats are concentrated in areas with the highest ST population share, SC seats are spread and rotated at delimitation, and reserved constituencies have a common electorate of all voters.
tq: Combine location, rotation and electorate principles in one reservation question.
sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

s: Which one of the following statements regarding Article 334 is correct?
o: The original period of reservation was 5 years and it ended in 1955.
The Article deals exclusively with reservation in local bodies.
The provision originally applied for 20 years, up to 1970, without later extension.
The original period of reservation was 10 years, up to 1960, and it has been repeatedly extended.
x: Article 334 originally provided for a ten-year period, up to 1960, and the reservation period has been repeatedly extended by constitutional amendments.
tq: Use the original time limit and the subsequent-extension feature together.
sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

s:
Which of the following statements about Anglo-Indian representation is correct?
1. The President could nominate two Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha.
2. The Governor could nominate one Anglo-Indian to a State Legislative Assembly.
3. These provisions were ended by the 104th Constitutional Amendment.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Articles 331 and 333 provided for nomination of two Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha by the President and one to a State Assembly by the Governor. The 104th Amendment ended these provisions.
tq: Check the authority, number and constitutional termination together.
sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

s:
The constitutional provision for reservation of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies under the 106th Amendment provides for which of the following?
1. One-third reservation of seats
2. Reservation for 15 years
3. Rotation after each delimitation
4. Immediate operation irrespective of census and delimitation
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The 106th Amendment provides one-third reservation for 15 years, with rotation after each delimitation. Its operation begins only after the next census and delimitation; therefore statement 4 is false.
tq: Spot the false immediacy claim in a statement about commencement of constitutional reservation.
sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

s: A constituency having no fixed geographical boundary, such as the Sangha seat in Sikkim, is known as a:
x: A floating constituency has no fixed geographical boundary. The Sangha constituency in Sikkim is an example in which only registered Buddhist monks vote and contest.
tq: Identify the exact electoral term from its defining geographical feature.
sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

s:
With reference to the Sangha constituency in Sikkim, consider the following statements:
1. It is an example of a floating constituency.
2. Only registered Buddhist monks can vote and contest in it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Sangha seat has no fixed geographical boundary and is restricted to registered Buddhist monks as electors and candidates.
tq: Test both defining features of a special constituency rather than just its name.
sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

s:
Match the type of election with its description:

List-I
A. General election
B. Mid-term election
C. By-election

List-II
1. Election to a legislature dissolved before expiry of its normal term
2. Election held for a single vacancy, ordinarily within six months
3. Election held at the normal end of the legislature’s term

sec: Reserved and special constituencies - SC/ST seats, floating constituencies

s: Under Section 80 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, an election can be called in question only by means of:
o: A writ petition before the District Court
A reference by the Election Commission

sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

s: An election petition under Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, must ordinarily be presented within:
o: 45 days of the election of the returned candidate
60 days of the declaration of poll
30 days of the notification of election
90 days of the constitution of the House
x: Section 81 requires an election petition to be presented within 45 days of the election of the returned candidate.
tq: Separate the 45-day filing period from the separate Section 80 rule and Section 100 grounds.
sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

s: Which court ordinarily tries an election petition under the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
o: Supreme Court in the first instance
x: Under Section 80A, an election petition is tried by the High Court. An appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
tq: Identify the court of original trial and distinguish it from the appellate court.
sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

s:
Consider the following grounds for declaring an election void under Section 100 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951:
1. The returned candidate was not qualified or was disqualified.
2. A corrupt practice was committed.
3. A nomination was improperly rejected.
4. Improper acceptance of votes or breach of the Constitution or the Act affected the result.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four circumstances are recognised grounds under Section 100 for declaring an election void, subject to the statutory requirements concerning their effect on the election result where applicable.
tq: Test the complete statutory list of grounds rather than relying on a single familiar ground.
sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

s: Which one of the following statements regarding disposal of election petitions is correct?
o: The Supreme Court tries every election petition directly and no appeal is permitted.
The Election Commission must decide the petition within six months, with no appeal.
The District Court must decide the petition within three months, with appeal to the High Court.
The High Court is required to try to decide the petition within six months, and an appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
x: The High Court should try to decide an election petition within six months, and an appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
tq: Use the court hierarchy and time expectation to reject authority swaps.
sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the present legal location of electoral offences such as bribery, undue influence and personation?
o: They remain in IPC Chapter IXA only.
They are contained in BNS Chapter IX, Sections 169 to 177, from 1 July 2024.
They are dealt with only under Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
They are contained in the Constitution under Article 329(b).
x: From 1 July 2024, electoral offences such as bribery, undue influence and personation are placed in Chapter IX of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Sections 169–177. Earlier, they were in Chapter IXA of the IPC.

sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

s:

List-I
A. Section 80
B. Section 80A
C. Section 81
D. Section 100

List-II
1. Grounds for declaring an election void
2. Petition to be presented within 45 days
3. No election may be called in question except by an election petition

sec: Election petitions - RPA 1951 Section 81, court, grounds

s:

s:

s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the first-past-the-post system used for Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections?

The candidate securing a majority of all registered voters wins.
The candidate securing the highest number of votes in a single-member constituency wins.

Consider the following statements regarding the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026:
1. It proposed raising the Lok Sabha ceiling from 550 to 850.
2. It proposed delimitation on the basis of the 2011 Census.
3. It was passed by the Lok Sabha with the required special majority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Bill proposed increasing the Lok Sabha ceiling from 550 to 850 and conducting delimitation on the 2011 Census. It was defeated, not passed with the required special majority.
tq: Identify the false outcome statement while retaining the two substantive proposals.

s: Why have southern States expressed apprehension regarding population-based delimitation?
o: They oppose the use of electronic voting machines in parliamentary elections.
They fear that States such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan may gain seats at their expense.
They fear that the Rajya Sabha will become a directly elected chamber.
They fear that all Lok Sabha seats reserved for Scheduled Castes will be abolished.
x: Southern States fear that population-based delimitation would transfer political representation towards more populous States such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan.
tq: Link the policy principle of population-based delimitation with its regional representation effect.

s: The EAC-PM proposal of August 2026 relating to Lok Sabha representation envisaged which of the following?
o: Increasing the Lok Sabha ceiling directly from 550 to 850 without changing constituencies
Merging 170 constituencies to reduce the Lok Sabha to 543 seats
Splitting 170 oversized constituencies to reach 824 seats
x: The EAC-PM proposal envisaged splitting 170 oversized constituencies in order to reach a total of 824 Lok Sabha seats.
tq: Check both components of the proposal—the number of constituencies and the proposed total.

s: With reference to delimitation and Andhra Pradesh–Telangana representation, which one of the following is correct?
o: The increase in seats under Section 26 awaits the census after 2026.
The increase in seats under Section 26 is unrelated to any future census.
Section 26 concerns only the abolition of reserved seats in Andhra Pradesh.
The increase in seats under Section 26 was completed on the basis of the 2001 Census.
x: The Andhra Pradesh–Telangana seat increase under Section 26 awaits the census conducted after 2026.
tq: Match the statutory reference with the qualifying time condition instead of treating the provision as immediately operative.

s: In State of Karnataka v. Prathik Parasrampuria (2026), removal of black money from elections was described as which of the following?

An exclusive duty of the Finance Commission
